name: Sistemi IoT
description: Basso consumo, sicurezza, aggiornamenti e cloud dei dispositivi connessi.

terms.definition: The current a device uses while it sleeps.
terms.example: The sleep current is two microamps with the RTC running.

terms.definition: The lowest power state, where almost everything is off.
terms.example: In deep sleep only the wake-up pin is active.

terms.definition: How long the device takes to become active after a wake-up event.
terms.example: The wake-up latency is under five microseconds.

terms.definition: Powering a device with energy from the environment, like light or vibration.
terms.example: The tag runs on energy harvesting from indoor light.

terms.definition: A small round battery, like a CR2032.
terms.example: The sensor runs for five years on a coin cell.

terms.definition: How long a device works before the battery is empty.
terms.example: We estimated the battery life from the average current.

terms.definition: A firmware update sent over the air.
terms.example: The OTA update is downloaded in the background.

terms.definition: Going back to the previous firmware if the new one fails.
terms.example: The bootloader does a rollback if the new image does not start.

terms.definition: Checking that the firmware is signed and authentic before running it.
terms.example: Secure boot rejects any image without a valid signature.

terms.definition: The part of the chip that is trusted by design and protects the keys.
terms.example: The keys are stored in the hardware root of trust.

terms.definition: The secret value used to encrypt and decrypt data.
terms.example: Each device has its own encryption key.

terms.definition: The unique, secure identity of each device.
terms.example: The device identity is created in the factory.

terms.definition: A digital document that proves the identity of a device or server.
terms.example: The certificate expires in ten years.

terms.definition: The protocol that encrypts data between a device and a server.
terms.example: All the traffic to the cloud uses TLS.

terms.definition: A lightweight publish-subscribe protocol for IoT messages.
terms.example: The sensors publish their data with MQTT.

terms.definition: The server that receives MQTT messages and sends them to subscribers.
terms.example: The broker handles ten thousand devices.

terms.definition: Data that devices send regularly about their state.
terms.example: The telemetry includes temperature and battery level.

terms.definition: The servers that store and process the device data.
terms.example: The cloud backend stores one year of data.

terms.definition: Processing data on or near the device instead of in the cloud.
terms.example: With edge computing, only the alarms go to the cloud.

terms.definition: Combining data from several sensors to get a better result.
terms.example: Sensor fusion combines the accelerometer and the gyroscope.

terms.definition: A sensor that measures acceleration and movement.
terms.example: The accelerometer wakes the device when it moves.

terms.definition: Adjusting a sensor so its readings are accurate.
terms.example: Each humidity sensor needs a calibration at the end of the line.

terms.definition: How many bits per second are sent.
terms.example: We lowered the data rate to increase the range.

terms.definition: The ability of a device to connect to a network.
terms.example: Connectivity problems are the first cause of support calls.

terms.definition: Monitoring and updating many devices in the field.
terms.example: Fleet management shows which devices need an update.

terms.definition: A failure that happens at the customer's site.
terms.example: We analyzed the field failure with the device logs.

terms.definition: Investigating problems on a device without touching it.
terms.example: Remote debugging saved us a trip to the customer.

terms.definition: A virtual model of a physical device, kept in sync with it.
terms.example: The digital twin shows the last known state of the pump.

terms.definition: The estimate of how much energy each part of the system uses.
terms.example: The radio takes eighty percent of the power budget.

terms.definition: Turning a part on only for short periods to save energy.
terms.example: Duty cycling the sensor reduced the current by ninety percent.

terms.definition: A drop of the supply voltage below the safe level.
terms.example: The brownout detector resets the MCU when the battery is low.

terms.definition: The ability of devices from different vendors to work together.
terms.example: We tested interoperability with five phone models.
